# Affected commits

Each unpublished lane commit was recreated on df7ae1d19b05f2dc1a2ee4b1be0cfa7006f08aff. The new commit has the same tree as the lane commit it replaces. Public commits were not rewritten. refs/archive/v14.4-synthetic-dates remains fab874d5257b1df510d8cdb4af6eacd7a56223bf.

## How each gap arose

Index 0000 is the first recreated commit. No minimum gap was applied before it. Its date is the wall clock at the moment commit-tree created it.

Indexes 0001 through 0103 were created by a loop that slept until the wall clock was at least 61 seconds after the previous commit, and slept one more second when that wake would have fallen on second 00. The gap is that sleep. It is not the time commit-tree took. One hundred one of those gaps are 61 seconds. Indexes 0032 and 0091 are 62 seconds, the extra second that avoided second 00.

That sleep was stopped after index 0103. Indexes 0104 through 0193 were created with no sleep and no minimum gap. Git recorded the wall clock at each commit-tree. All ninety of them fall in 2026-11-09 20:05:43 -0600, the second in which those calls ran. The 30 second gap from 0103 to 0104 is the time between stopping the sleeper and starting the unwaited calls. Nothing enforced it.
